title: MCF3M Module 4 — quadratic vertex form (L1) and completing the square (L2)

process_slots.name: Compare two equivalent writings of one model; decide which shows the vertex; verify by algebra and by table/graph
Inspect vertex form: vertex (h, k) including plus-inside, axis x = h, maximum or minimum from the sign of a
Predict what changing one of a, h, or k will do, then check the graph and the rewritten equation
Expand vertex form into standard form and verify equivalent representations with graphing technology
Describe what can be read from vertex form compared with standard form and factored form, without producing those other writings
Complete the square with algebra tiles or an area diagram (a = 1, integer b) so the completed square and leftover constant are visible before algebra
Algebraically complete the square for f(x) = x^2 + bx + c (a = 1) to produce (x − h)^2 + k
When a ≠ 1, factor a from the x^2 and x terms before completing the square, then finish to a(x − h)^2 + k
Complete the square when b/a is a simple rational (Ministry e.g. ½, 0.75), as variation after integer cases
After producing vertex form, verify with graphing technology that standard and vertex writings are equivalent representations
From standard form, complete the square to obtain vertex, axis, and max/min, then sketch those key features only (A2.11 light)
Choose a suitable sketch strategy — completing the square for the vertex, or factoring when intercepts are friendly — with criteria (light; no formula)
On one shared quadratic, reverse Lesson 1 expand (vertex→standard) with completing the square (standard→vertex) and confirm both directions leave the graph unchanged (A2.7 review only)
